title: LLM runner: embed a lightweight Go LLM client for the ladder's budgeted agent stage — non-streaming completions, per-call budgets (tokens+wall-clock), config-driven model + fallback chain, context-compaction hook
description: the maintainer directive 09-16: lightweight LLM framework, avoid wastefulness — the daemon runs under stress, so STREAMING IS A NON-GOAL (one buffered request/response per stage; a hung stream is the failure mode we refuse). description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, reproduced twice on the control host. With examples/config.toml (which sets no dashboard.token_file) the daemon boots and serves :7644, but `trouble dashboard token create` mints a tdt_ token that the SAME daemon rejects: GET /incidents -> 401 {"error":{"code":"TROUBLE-DASHBOARD-002","message":"authentication failed"}} - on a daemon started AFTER the token existed. The token hash in ~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json matches sha256(plaintext) exactly (verified), so mint and store agree; the daemon simply never loaded the file. Mechanism: dashboard.DefaultConfig() TokenFile = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json" (internal/dashboard/config.go:58, a literal tilde); internal/app/dashdeps.go:43 only overrides it when the lifecycle key is non-empty; nothing expands ~ inside the dashboard package, os.Stat fails, and tokens.go readFileIntoSet documents "a missing file yields a valid empty set" - so it fails closed, silently, forever. Proof of the mechanism: with the identical build, config and token, adding `token_file = "~/.config/trouble/dashboard-tokens.json"` to [dashboard] and restarting flips GET /incidents from 401 to 200 rendering "Incidents - trouble" (15 KB). Blast radius: the dashboard (SPEC-10) is unreachable and the ONLY credential the product can mint is inert, on the documented config path; tests/e2e/cli_smoke.sh passes only because it hands the daemon an absolute token_file. Fix direction: expand ~ (or resolve the path through the same resolver the CLI uses) in DefaultConfig/dashboardConfig, and log a WARN whenever the token store loads as missing/empty so the failure is not silent.

Booting examples/config.toml writes a `subsystem_not_built` lifecycle record per refused subsystem on EVERY boot (12 records across 4 boots): sentinel: "no sentinel projects configured" (internal/app/subsystems.go:386 buildSentinel returns nil for len(projects)==0); issues: "TROUBLE-ISSUES-003: config_invalid: driver github needs owner and repo (SPEC-09 3.9.1)"; skills: "TROUBLE-SKILLS-001: config_invalid: exactly one of source_path or source_url must be set". Consequences observed: (a) nothing ever listens on ingest.bind 127.0.0.1:7643 - POST /api/1/event/ is connection-refused, so the README's headline on-ramp ("POST /api/{id}/event/, one curl from any runtime") is impossible; (b) /health.json returns status="degraded" with detail={"sensor_degraded":"inotify"} - it names a sensor, never the three absent subsystems, and has no `subsystems` key at all; (c) the dashboard surfaces nothing either, so the documented "absent means no such record" rule only works if an operator knows to grep the ledger; (d) boot exits 0 and the daemon serves, so nothing looks wrong. There is also no documented (or implemented) way to declare a project: no CLI verb, no config key reachable through `trouble config explain` - sentinel's project set is only ever passed in-process (SubsystemOptions.SentinelProjects), so an operator cannot enable the ingest plane at all. Fix direction: populate SentinelProjects from config ([[projects]] with id/public_key/secret), surface a `subsystems` block (name, built, refusal code) in /health.json + the dashboard, and make the README's on-ramp example reachable from the shipped example config. LATER SAME RUN (sharper evidence): with a rules.d installed (examples/rules/10-defaults.toml copied to <state_root>/../config/rules.d/) the daemon reports /health.json status="ok" with detail=null and all six sensors degraded=false - while the same boot's ledger still carries the three subsystem_not_built records (sentinel: no sentinel projects configured; issues: TROUBLE-ISSUES-003; skills: TROUBLE-SKILLS-001). So the health surface does not merely under-describe a degraded boot: on a clean-shaped config it issues a GREEN light for an instance whose ingest plane, issue desk and skill loop are absent. That is the project's own named anti-pattern ("never observe itself into a green lie") reproduced on the health surface, and it is why this row is P0.

description: Dogfood 2026-09-17, measured on a throwaway state root against the live control host (idle, loadavg ~7 but no app activity). Fold the same fix as (1): source these values from the accessors that already answer correctly elsewhere.

title: [P2] Boot READY cost is a SPEC-01/SPEC-03 decision: 92% of a quiet boot is the D-Bus startup reconcile writing 80-122 SEQUENTIAL ledger records, each paying its own group-commit window + fdatasync (measured: 17.2s quiet vs 44.4s of fsync waiting under fleet I/O load) - decide batch-append for the reconcile, or move it off the READY path
description: Filed by the plus-ultra release from TRBL-025's measured attribution (not a guess): internal/app boot READY latency is dominated by sensors_start, whose D-Bus startup reconcile emits one ledger record per failed systemd unit (plus config dump, 3 subsystem refusals, capability probe). Writers are SEQUENTIAL, so no coalescing happens: N records = N group-commit windows (ledger.fsync_window_ms = 200ms default) + N fdatasyncs. Measured on this host: 89 sync calls totalling 1.44s (median 5.5ms) on a quiet volume vs 262 calls totalling 44.41s (median 143ms, p95 353ms, max 1.99s) while other fleet writers hit the same device; a 4KB fsync probe goes 3.6ms -> 19.5ms median. That is the whole 'load stretch' - it is not process sharing (isolated vs in-suite at equal conditions differs by 0.02s). DECISION NEEDED (SPEC-01 §3.5 durable-on-return vs SPEC-03 §3.3 per-unit incident model): either (a) give the reconcile a BATCH append path that writes K records in ONE group-commit window while keeping the durable-on-return contract per batch, or (b) move the startup reconcile off the READY path (READY first, reconcile in the background, with an explicit health/ledger marker that the reconcile is still pending) - and say which contract wins when the two conflict. A host with zero failed units boots ~1.5s, so the size of the win is endpoint-dependent (60-122 records here) and must be stated as such. Verify with the OnBootPhase phase table (TRBL-025 landed it) before/after, plus the sequential-append ledger test. Do NOT trade away durability for latency without saying so in the spec.
